First, calculate the mass of ethanol:
\[ \text{Mass of ethanol} = \text{Density of ethanol} \times \text{Volume of ethanol} = 0.789 \, \text{g/cm}^3 \times 50 \, \text{cm}^3 = 39.45 \, \text{g} \]

Next, calculate the mass of octane:
\[ \text{Mass of octane} = \text{Density of octane} \times \text{Volume of octane} = 0.703 \, \text{g/cm}^3 \times 950 \, \text{cm}^3 = 667.85 \, \text{g} \]

Now, calculate the moles of ethanol and octane using their respective molar masses:
- Molar mass of ethanol (\( \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} \)): 46.08 g/mol
- Molar mass of octane (\( \text{C}_8\text{H}_{18} \)): 114.22 g/mol

Moles of ethanol:
\[ \text{Moles of ethanol} = \frac{39.45 \, \text{g}}{46.08 \, \text{g/mol}} = 0.856 \, \text{mol} \]

Moles of octane:
\[ \text{Moles of octane} = \frac{667.85 \, \text{g}}{114.22 \, \text{g/mol}} = 5.847 \, \text{mol} \]

Calculate the energy released from burning each component:
- Enthalpy of combustion of ethanol: -1276 kJ/mol
- Enthalpy of combustion of octane: -5144 kJ/mol

Energy from ethanol:
\[ \text{Energy from ethanol} = 0.856 \, \text{mol} \times (-1276 \, \text{kJ/mol}) = -1092.256 \, \text{kJ} \]

Energy from octane:
\[ \text{Energy from octane} = 5.847 \, \text{mol} \times (-5144 \, \text{kJ/mol}) = -30080.568 \, \text{kJ} \]

Sum the energies to find the total energy released:
\[ \text{Total energy released} = -1092.256 \, \text{kJ} + (-30080.568 \, \text{kJ}) = -31172.824 \, \text{kJ} \]
